questions.question: A sum of ₹8,200 was divided among A, B and C such that A had ₹500 more than B and C had ₹300 more than A. How much was C's share (in ₹)? ₹8,200
questions.solution:
Everything here is described with respect to B, 
so take B as the base. 
A = B + 500        C = A + 300 = B + 800 
 Step 1   Add the three shares and equate to the 
given total. 
B + (B + 500) + (B + 800) = 8,200   ⇒  3B + 1,300 
= 8,200   ∴  B = ₹2,300 
 Step 2   Come back to what was asked — C, not 
B. 
C = B + 800 = 2,300 + 800 = ₹3,100

questions.solution:
A ratio is given, so use ONE letter — the numbers 
are 3k and 5k, never x and y. 
 Step 1

 Step 2    
3k + 5k = 8k = 8 × 8 = 64

questions.question: Atul purchased bread costing ₹20 and gave a ₹100 note. The shopkeeper returned balance in coins of ₹2, ₹5 and ₹10 in ratio 5:4:1. How many ₹5 coins did he give?
Hridaya found coins of ₹1, ₹2, ₹5 and ₹10 in ratio 10:5:2:1. If there are 72 coins in all, how much money (₹) was in the piggy bank? ş
questions.solution:
Two different things are counted here — the 
NUMBER of coins and their VALUE. Count first. 
 Step 1   The counts are 10k, 5k, 2k, k. 
10k + 5k + 2k + k = 18k = 72   ∴  k = 4 
 Step 2   Now the value — multiply every count by 
its denomination. 
1(10k) + 2(5k) + 5(2k) + 10(k) = 10k + 10k + 10k + 
10k = 40k 
Value = 40 × 4 = ₹160

questions.question: If (6x + 5y):(6x – 5y) = 11:5, find x:y.
questions.solution:
The SUM and the DIFFERENCE of the same two 
terms are given — that is exactly where 
componendo–dividendo is used. 
 Step 1   Apply it :  if p / q = m / n  then  (p + q) / (p 
− q) = (m + n) / (m − n). 
[(6x+5y) + (6x−5y)] / [(6x+5y) − (6x−5y)] = (11 + 5) 
/ (11 − 5) 
12x / 10y = 16 / 6   ⇒   6x / 5y = 8 / 3 
 Step 2   Cross-multiply and reduce. 
18x = 40y    ∴  x : y = 40 : 18 = 20 : 9

questions.question: Three friends A, B, and C have money in the ratio 2:3:4 summing to ₹81. If they each receive an equal amount x, their new ratio becomes 4:5:6. Find x. (CGL 2025)
questions.solution:
The same amount x goes to each friend, so the 
total rises by 3x — 4 : 5 : 6 does not sit on ₹81. 
 Step 1   Fix the present shares from 2 : 3 : 4. 
2 + 3 + 4 = 9 units = ₹81   ⇒  1 unit = ₹9   ∴  A = 
18,  B = 27,  C = 36 
 Step 2   Add x to any TWO of them and match 
the new ratio. 
(18 + x) / (27 + x) = 4 / 5   ⇒  90 + 5x = 108 + 4x   ∴  
x = ₹18

B = 4 × 4,000 = ₹16,000

questions.question: The expenses for a college picnic are partly fixed and partly variable. Charge is ₹400/head for 15 people and ₹300/head for 30 people. Find charge/head for 75 people.
questions.solution:
“Partly fixed, partly variable” always means  
Total = Fixed + (people × Variable). 
 Step 1   Turn each per-head charge into a TOTAL 
expense. 
15 people :  15 × 400 = ₹6,000 = F + 15V 
30 people :  30 × 300 = ₹9,000 = F + 30V 
 Step 2   Subtract — F disappears. 
15V = 3,000   ∴  V = ₹200        F = 6,000 − 15(200) 
= ₹3,000 
 Step 3   Put 75 people into the same model. 
Total = 3,000 + 75 × 200 = ₹18,000   ∴  per head 
= 18,000 ÷ 75 = ₹240

questions.question: Total expenses of a boarding house are partly fixed and partly varying. Avg expense/boarder is ₹700 for 25 boarders and ₹600 for 50 boarders. Find avg expense for 100 boarders.
questions.solution:
Same model as the previous question :  Total = 
Fixed + (boarders × Variable). 
 Step 1   Turn the averages into totals. 
25 boarders :  25 × 700 = ₹17,500 = F + 25V 
50 boarders :  50 × 600 = ₹30,000 = F + 50V 
 Step 2   Subtract. 
25V = 12,500   ∴  V = ₹500        F = 17,500 − 12,500 
= ₹5,000 
 Step 3   Now 100 boarders. 
Total = 5,000 + 100 × 500 = ₹55,000   ∴  average 
= ₹550

questions.question: Aman has ₹20 and ₹10 notes amounting to ₹390. If numbers are interchanged, new amount is ₹90 less. Find number of ₹20 notes.
questions.solution:
Interchanging the notes changes the amount, so 
write BOTH amounts in the same two letters. 
Let a = number of ₹20 notes,   b = number of 
₹10 notes 
 Step 1   Original amount, then the interchanged 
one. 
20a + 10b = 390          10a + 20b = 390 − 90 = 300 
 Step 2   Divide both by 10 to keep the numbers 
small. 
2a + b = 39   …(i)          a + 2b = 30   …(ii) 
 Step 3   2×(i) − (ii) clears b. 
4a + 2b = 78   and   a + 2b = 30   ⇒  3a = 48   ∴  a 
= 16

questions.question: A rabbit takes 8 leaps for every 5 leaps of a rat, and distance covered by rat in 5 leaps = distance by rabbit in 4 leaps. Find ratio of their speeds.
questions.solution:
Speed = (leaps taken in a given time) × (length of 
one leap). The question gives both, separately. 
 Step 1   Leap RATE — straight from the first line. 
rabbit : rat  =  8 : 5   leaps in the same time 
 Step 2   Leap LENGTH — from the distance line. 
5 × (rat leap) = 4 × (rabbit leap)   ∴  rat leap : 
rabbit leap = 4 : 5 
 Step 3   Multiply rate by length for each animal. 
rabbit = 8 × 5 = 40        rat = 5 × 4 = 20    ∴  40 : 
20 = 2 : 1

questions.question: Deepak spends 75% of his income; Karan spends 80% of his income. Both save ₹7,500 each. Sanjay's income is 1/3 of (Deepak + Karan's income). If Sanjay spends 7/9 of his income, find his savings. (CGL 2025)
questions.solution:
The savings are given, not the incomes — so read 
each income BACKWARDS from its savings 
percentage. 
 Step 1   Deepak spends 75%, so he saves 25%. 
25% of income = ₹7,500   ∴  Deepak = ₹30,000 
 Step 2   Karan spends 80%, so he saves 20%. 
20% of income = ₹7,500   ∴  Karan = ₹37,500 
 Step 3   Sanjay is one-third of the two together. 
Sanjay = ⅓ × (30,000 + 37,500) = ⅓ × 67,500 = 
₹22,500 
 Step 4   He spends 7/9, so he saves 2/9. 
Savings = 2/9 × 22,500 = ₹5,000
